papers_read.title_as_printed: Differential Role for Hippocampal Subfields in Alzheimer's Disease Progression Revealed with Deep Learning (Kwak et al., Cerebral Cortex 2022)
TASNet: A tri-modal attentive scale robust adaptive fusion framework for progressive mild cognitive impairment classification (Zhu et al., J. Neurosci. Methods 2026)

what_each_reports.P-182: DenseNet on a 3D bounding box of baseline T1 hippocampal voxels, trained only on AD vs CN (ADNI-2/GO) and applied without retraining to MCI; test set 381 ADNI-2/GO MCI (118 pMCI, 263 sMCI) labelled on diagnoses at least 18 months apart; Acc 75.85%, AUC 0.777, sens 0.66, spec 0.80.
what_each_reports.P-23: TASNet trained end-to-end on sMCI vs pMCI from baseline sMRI + FDG-PET + CSF (Abeta42, tau, p-tau), 36-month criterion, ADNI1/ADNI2; 8:1:1 split of 200 MCI, so the test set is about 20 subjects (sens 83.33% = 10/12, spec 87.50% = 7/8); Acc 85.00%, AUC 0.9167. Its own sMRI-only ablation: Acc 65.00%, AUC 0.6667.

quantity_a: Accuracy of a hippocampus-only sMRI model transferred from AD/CN training, on 381 MCI (progression across a follow-up of at least 18 months), single held-out cohort.
quantity_b: Accuracy of a tri-modal (sMRI + FDG-PET + CSF) model trained on MCI labels (36-month criterion), on a held-out test split of about 20 MCI subjects.
incompatible_if_same: No. On about 20 test subjects, 17/20 = 85% has a binomial 95% interval of roughly 62-97%, which contains 75.85%. P-23's own sMRI-only configuration scores 65%, below P-182, so no ordering in favour of either input is contradicted.

gates.task: match nominally (T2), but the horizons differ (at least 18 months vs 36 months).
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI in both (ADNI-2/GO vs ADNI1+ADNI2); overlap possible.
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal ADNI held-out testing.
gates.modality_family: mismatch, not waived: P-182 is structural MRI only; P-23 adds FDG-PET and CSF fluid biomarkers. The record's 'Yes / structural_mri' is wrong for P-23.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric (accuracy) but different predictor set (sMRI vs sMRI+PET+CSF), different training target (AD/CN transfer vs direct pMCI/sMCI), different horizon, and test sets differing twentyfold in size.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.85 and 0.7585 are below 0.97. P-23's test set of about 20 subjects makes its point estimate imprecise.
independence: Distinct author groups; both ADNI (ADNI-2 MCI may appear in both).
grounds: The predictor sets differ: P-23's 85% needs FDG-PET and CSF alongside sMRI, and its sMRI-only arm reaches 65%; P-182 uses only hippocampal sMRI. The modality gate fails and is not waived.
The endpoints differ (progression over a follow-up of at least 18 months vs a 36-month criterion), and P-182's model never saw MCI labels in training.
The two accuracies are compatible in any case: P-23's roughly 20-subject test set gives an interval that contains 75.85%.

record_defects: modality_family_equal 'Yes' with 'structural_mri' is wrong: P-23 is sMRI + FDG-PET + CSF.
The registry Sample_N_Approx for P-23 is '119'; the PDF gives 552 in total, 200 MCI (82 pMCI, 118 sMCI), with a test split of about 20.
The registry Modality 'MRI/PET' for P-23 omits CSF; for P-182 'MRI/PET' is wrong (sMRI only).

resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (Acc); Gap magnitude 0.092 exceeds threshold' without regard to predictor set or test-set size; the resolution field says 'Rejected - false positive' while the status is partially_resolved_candidate.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Both studies reporting the same predictor set (for example sMRI only) on the same horizon, with test sets large enough that the intervals exclude each other.
